topology: real two-machine (Host A gateway -> Azure Host B worker/db/redis)
interpretation: OBSERVED: a real packet-level partition between Host A and Host B (iptables DROP on Host B targeting Host A's actual public IP, inserted and removed over SSH) blocked Postgres/Redis reachability during the window; the gateway's own already-authorized requests and queued events were not lost (Redis/Postgres on Host B retained state) and reconciled once the DROP rule was removed.
superseded_note: This run used an in-VM iptables -I DOCKER-USER DROP rule as the partition mechanism. That mechanism was directly verified AFTER this run to be a silent no-op on this Docker/Ubuntu 24.04 host (0 packets/bytes matched; a live connection succeeded straight through it) due to a Docker/nftables backend mismatch -- the rule never actually blocked anything, so drop_rule_added being true here does not mean a real partition occurred.
